bosses.name: Abductor Virgin
bosses.summary:
Abductor Virgin is an enemy in Elden Ring.

===Overview===
Abductor Virgins are automatons affiliated with the Volcano Manor. Originally designed with the intent of capturing and transposing victims for interrogation, they can be found strewn around the Lands Between. Though the majority have lost their powers of transposition, they will still attempt to fulfill their original directive if approached.

To aid in their task, Abductor Virgins have been outfitted with heavy weaponry on both arms that alter how they approach each target. When a Virgin has approached a target, they will open their chest cavity and attempt to pull them in with serpentine tendrils. Given the loss of their transposition ability, the target will be constricted instead. If they survive this, they will be spat back out.

They are weak to Lightning damage and all damage taken is greatly increased if attacked when their chest cavity is opened during a charge or attempted grab.

It can also use abilities reminiscent of other animals- hopping like a rabbit, charging like a boar, or curling into a ball and rolling like a goat.

fight_notes: [Bosses]
[Background]
A lone Cleanrot Knight, encountered in an alcove at the very end of Stillwater Cave that has been partially flooded in poisonous waters.
[Strategy]
Most of the room is full of poisonous water so it's advisable to quickly run to the small island of safety just left of the boss, in the middle left to far left section of the room.

Since this boss is the spear-wielding variant and this fight will most likely happen early in the game it's extremely important to avoid its Scarlet Rot-inducing, charging grab attack (signified by its spear glowing a bright gold). This is most easily done by rolling diagonally forward to get to the other side of the boss. Since the boss is vulnerable to backstabs this is a good moment to try and get one.
[Background]

A Cleanrot Knight and its commander, both encountered in an alcove at the very end of Abandoned Cave that has been partially flooded by scarlet rot. The remains of numerous Abductor Virgins lay scattered around the arena.
[Strategy]

As the fight starts only the spear-wielder is present, with the scythe-wielding commander rising from the rot pool to the left within 12 seconds of starting the fight. As such it is best to spend that opening either summmoning a Spirit or rushing down the spear knight to try and at least severely wound it before the scythe knight can join the fray.

Of the two combatants, the spear knight is more aggressive and will try to restrict player movement with its Sacred Phalanx and inflict Scarlet Rot with its charge while the scythe knight will harass from afar with Miquella's Ring of Light and buff both of them with a unique combination of health regeneration and extra Fire resistance to cover for one of their weaknesses.
If fighting alone, try to pull the spear knight to the right so that the hill blocks the light rings and buy extra time to kill it.

bosses.name: Dragonlord Placidusax
bosses.summary: Dragonlord Placidusax is a boss in Elden Ring, encountered in Crumbling Farum Azula.
fight_notes: [Moveset]
[Phase 1]

Placidusax will begin the fight by summoning a storm of red lightning bolts which rain down on the arena for a few seconds. During his first phase, he will primarily use lightning claw attacks if the player is in front, a slam attack with his wings if they are to either side, and a tail sweep if they get behind him. He also has fire breath attacks which cover a large area in front of or around him. He has an area of effect attack which involves summoning a large lightning bolt and thrusting it into the ground, creating a massive explosion after a short delay. When he performs this attack, the music will briefly get quieter and red waves will emanate from where the lightning bolt hits, providing an indicator for the range of the explosion.
[Phase 2]

Placidusax now gains the ability to disappear in a cloud of fog. If he floats into the air before doing so, he will reappear in a stationary or moving thundercloud above the arena, before emerging and diving down at the player. He also gains the ability to disappear and reappear in quick succession, unleashing attacks with his lightning claws in between.
[Environment]

The arena is a large, circular platform with pillars dotted around the outside. These can be destroyed by Placidusax's attacks. The size of the arena gives ample room to avoid his area of effect or dodge his divebomb attacks.
[Notes]

Placidusax shows serious signs of damage on his body. Notably he is missing three of his five heads and second pair of wings, in spite of the Old Lord's Talisman showing just four with complete wings.
→ Their location:
Part of a dragon’s body (an arm, wing, and head) resembling Placidusax can be seen sticking out of a body of rock in Farum Azula prior to reaching his arena.
According to the Remembrance of the Dragonlord, Placidusax was an Elden Lord before the era of the Erdtree, making him the earliest known Elden Lord.
Placidusax's design is most likely modeled after King Ghidorah.

bosses.name: Elden Beast
bosses.summary: Elden Beast is the final boss of Elden Ring. It is encountered inside the Erdtree in Leyndell, Ashen Capital.
fight_notes: Elden Beast is the second half of the final boss fight, with Radagon of the Golden Order as the first half. Unlike the former fight, it is possible to summon Torrent for this fight.
[Moveset]

The Elden Beast uses a combination of physical sword attacks and golden Holy attacks. It will regularly swim away from the player, or disappear underwater before emerging, meaning that the fight often requires one to chase after the Elden Beast.

When its health reaches around 80% it will fly up into the air and create a golden ring which closes in on the player before exploding. This can be avoided by jumping over the ring as it closes in. It will also begin to use additional attacks, such as Elden Stars or Spear Showers.
At around 30% health, it will perform the Golden Ring attack again, but this time it will generate three rings that each close in on the player.
[Strategy]
Its normal sword attacks are fairly easy to dodge, with perhaps the repeating stabs being an exception.
The Golden Rings can be jumped over to preserve your momentum and get out of them quicker, while the Spear Showers can be avoid by running while zig-zagging.

Elden Stars, if it cannot be interrupted by a stagger, is quite dangerous due to the consistent damage over time it can inflict and because it will gain speed to chase if allowed to travel with minimal turning. A way to fairly easily dodge it is to circle the Elden Beast counter-clockwise (that is, heading around it to your right before circling left to run out the duration.
[Environment]
The arena is a large, flat body of shallow water. Although it appears endless, the arena does have invisible walls surrounding it.
[Notes]

It is heavily implied that the Elden Beast was the being who imprisoned Marika inside the Erdtree based on one of its attacks where it attempts to grab the player and lift them up in the air to crucify and then pierce them with a barrage of golden spears, similar to how Marika was seen in the cutscene before the final boss battle.

fight_notes: [Strategy]
Try to stick close to him as his ranged sword swipes are much wider and generally harder to predict.

It is possible to bait him into a cycle of repeated shield slams by getting behind him and only landing one attack (lighter weapons can possibly use an uncharged heavy attack and some skills are quick enough to also be used) after each slam. Be aware that he can also follow up with an explosion sometimes, so take a moment to see if the shield begins to glow red as he is about to pull it up.
The grab is rather hard to dodge and very delayed. Wait until his hand begins to move towards you before dodging. It is also possible to dodge by running far enough away or by being behind him.
The blade drill is hard to avoid if rolling to the right and has some reach so try to roll forward and to the left.
His shield charge is very quick so try to stay relatively close as to not provoke it.
[Bosses]
[Background]

Elemer is encountered in the hall at the top of the Shaded Castle. He can channel energy through his sword, allowing him to send it towards the player and control it at a distance, or fire a red beam by rotating it quickly.

The first time he is encountered he will be facing the painting at the end of the room, making a heavy initial attack such as a charged heavy attack more possible. On subsequent attempts he will be facing the entrance.
Warmaster's Shack=
[Background]

The Bell Bearing Hunter appears in Warmaster's Shack at night. He will only spawn if the player has talked to Knight Bernahl and exhausted his dialogue. Bernahl will not be present while the Bell Bearing Hunter is spawned, but will reappear if the player dies or if they defeat the boss.
[Background]

The Bell Bearing Hunter will appear inside the Church of Vows at night. To get him to spawn, speak to Miriel, Pastor of Vows and listen to all of his dialogue options. Miriel will not be present when the Bell Bearing Hunter appears, but will reappear if the player dies or if they defeat the boss.

bosses.summary: The Fire Giant is a boss in Elden Ring. He is encountered at Flame Peak on the Mountaintops of the Giants. This encounter is not optional as it must be completed to unlock Crumbling Farum Azula and advance the main storyline.

encounters.name: Fire Giant
encounters.weak_spot: Wounded right ankle (phase 1), Wrists and eye (phase 2); 2x damage

fight_notes: Alexander, Warrior Jar is available as a summon for this fight, provided he has been met at Mt. Gelmir. His summon sign is just inside the boss gate.
Torrent can be used during this fight.
; Environment

The arena is a large snowfield with craggy, uneven terrain. The field slops upwards from the entrance, and the Giant begins the fight at the top of the slope. Torrent can be called during this fight, and is useful for covering distance and avoiding the avalanche by jumping.
[Moveset]
[Phase 1]

During phase 1, the Fire Giant will fight using a large, circular dish. Although he is fairly slow-moving, he is able to cover distance using his roll. He also possesses the ability to launch an avalanche straight towards the player. Initially, the majority of his attacks involve slamming the dish into the ground.

The objective initially is to attack the red braids wrapped around his left leg. After enough damage has been dealt, the braids will fall off, uncovering his injured ankle. At this point he will roll three times in succession, and then reach into the mouth on his abdomen, coating his hand in flames. He now gains the ability to use two fire-based abilities- a fast-moving fireball, and a large, slow-moving fire orb that homes in on the player.
[Phase 2]

Once his health drops below 47%, a cutscene plays and phase 2 begins. The Fire Giant has now lost the large dish as well as his left leg, and is forced to kneel on the ground. He is less mobile during this phase, however he can still roll. He now has a greater variety of fire spells. He may summon pillars of fire that erupt from the ground around him, breathe fire, or spew molten rocks that rain down on the arena. His weak spot is now on his left forearm.

bosses.summary: Godrick the Grafted is a boss in Elden Ring. He is a Demigod and a Shardbearer who is encountered in Stormveil Castle.
fight_notes: Nepheli Loux, Warrior is available as a summon for this fight, as long as the player has spoken to her in Stormveil Castle. Her summon sign can be found just outside the arena.
[Moveset]
[Phase 1]

The fight begins following a cutscene. Godrick will primarily use his axe and his large left arm to deal damage, and can generate cyclones and earthquakes for area-of-effect damage. He can roll to cover ground quickly, and has a wind-based ranged homing attack.
[Phase 2]

Once Godrick's health reaches 60%, he will stop attacking the player and chop off his own arm. This is followed by a cutscene, which transitions into phase 2. Godrick can now spew fire from the dragon's head grafted to his left arm, providing him with more ranged and area-of-effect attacks.
[Environment]

The arena mainly consists of a narrow, paved area without any obstacles, lined on both sides by graveyards. There is a wider section at the arena's entrance, around the steps. It is possible to move between the gravestones, however doing so may reduce the player's ability to avoid Godrick's attacks.
[Notes]
Godrick is an optional boss, however he drops a Great Rune, two of which are required to enter Leyndell, Royal Capital.

In cut content, Gatekeeper Gostoc claimed to be a son of Godrick, and would be an alternative option to Nepheli Loux for lordship of Stormveil Castle after Godrick's defeat, after which he would succumb to the practice of grafting as well.

Damage types: mainly Standard damage, with some Pierce damage from its thrusts and Fire damage from its flame breaths.

It's immune to all Status Effects and has 40% negation to all non-Physical damage types except for Magic, where it has only 20% resistance. It is somewhat weak to Strike damage, having 0% negation towards it, and a mild 10% negation against all other Physical damage types.

Since it starts out lying on the ground and will take a few seconds to get up once alerted, it's easy to get in some opening hits on its ankles. It has the range advantage and can hit most of the cave thanks to the length of its weapon.

The simplest strategy is to do the same as with a regular, non-boss halberd golem by sticking behind its ankles and backing away when its starts hitting the ground with the butt of its weapon or if it breaths fire.

→ This female character appears only on horseback and demonstrates unmatched skill with the bow.

bosses.name: Malenia, Blade of Miquella
bosses.summary: Malenia, Blade of Miquella is an optional remembrance boss in Elden Ring. She is a Demigod Shardbearer who is encountered in Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree. She and her elder twin brother, Miquella of the Haligtree, are together known as the Twin Prodigies (天賦の双子, Tenpu no Futago).
fight_notes: Malenia is fought at the end of Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, in a large chamber beyond the Haligtree Roots Site of Grace.
Malenia will regain lost HP with every successful attack, even if they are blocked.
[Moveset]
[Phase 1 - Malenia, Blade of Miquella]

In phase 1, Malenia will primarily make use of melee attacks using her sword. Her quick attacks, combined with her HP regeneration on hit, mean that she can rapidly recover from any damage dealt. However, she staggers easily, and her attacks can be cancelled by attacking during her wind-up animations. Frostbite and Blood Loss are especially good for staggering her.
[Phase 2 - Malenia, Goddess of Rot]

Once her health reaches 0, a cutscene will play, instigating phase 2. Malenia, now with large wings, gains a variety of Scarlet Rot-based attacks, and many of her regular attacks can now inflict the status effect. She will begin the phase with 80% of her maximum health, but can recover this using her HP regeneration. This phase will always begin with a Scarlet Aeonia attack, which can immediately end the fight if the player does not immediately get some distance. She can also create phantom projections of herself, which will attack and then disappear.
[Environment]
Malenia's arena is a wide cavern with a shallow pool of water in the middle. There are no obstacles, so there is plenty of space to gain distance during some of Malenia's more devastating attacks.
[Notes]

Malenia has a prosthetic right arm, left leg, and right foot. It is unknown if these were amputated due to the scarlet rot festering in her body, or injuries obtained from battle. The rot has also visibly spread over her eyes, so she is presumably also blind. Neither seems to influence her battle prowess in the slightest, however.
According to the Scarlet Aeonia Incantation description, Malenia will become a Goddess if her scarlet flower blooms three times.
Malenia is among a group of few select enemies that need to be parried multiple times for a successful riposte, another being Radagon.

Once defeated, she will leave behind a large, solid Scarlet Aeonia in her arena. If the player has the Unalloyed Gold Needle after completing Millicent's questline, it can be given to the Aeonia to receive Miquella's Needle and an Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone

Millicent and her four sisters are implied to be descended from Malenia in some way, but more as offshoots, or buds, of her Scarlet Bloom rather than actual daughters. They are also referred to as Scarlet Valkyries.

bosses.name: Maliketh, the Black Blade
bosses.summary: Maliketh, the Black Blade is a boss in Elden Ring, encountered in Crumbling Farum Azula. This is not an optional boss as Maliketh must be defeated to unlock Leyndell, Ashen Capital and reach the endgame of Elden Ring.

encounters.name: Maliketh, the Black Blade – Beast Clergyman

fight_notes: [Moveset]
[Phase 1 - Beast Clergyman]

Phase 1 is much like combat against Gurranq. During this phase, the Beast Clergyman will make use of his Cinquedea as well as a variety of bestial incantations. His attacks are very fast, leaving few obvious spaces for the player to attack. He may use an earthquake attack, causing area of effect damage in a small circle around him.
[Phase 2 - Maliketh, the Black Blade]

At half health, a cutscene will play and phase 2 will begin. Maliketh now wields his Black Blade, and all of his attacks will cause rapid health loss overtime as well as temporary reduction of maximum health. Maliketh is a fast and acrobatic fighter, relying on quick slashes, spins and leaps. He will sometimes jump up and cling to the pillars around the arena, before either jumping at the player or jumping away and firing a ranged attack.

During this phase, the Blasphemous Claw can be used to deflect Maliketh's Black Blade attack, as well as the spin attack he performs after plunging his sword into the ground. These attacks can be identified with their golden glow when performed. Deflecting his attacks will stun him for a few seconds, creating a window during which to attack. He cannot be dealt a critical hit form this stun, only from stance break.
[Environment]

The arena is a wide, circular room. It is possible to fall off the edges all around the perimeter of the room. There are several pillars around the centre of the room, which Maliketh may jump onto to perform certain attacks. These pillars can also be used to create distance between oneself and Maliketh, or to avoid his ranged attacks.

bosses.name: Margit, the Fell Omen
bosses.summary: Margit the Fell Omen is a boss in Elden Ring.

encounters.name: Margit the Fell Omen
encounters.runes: Limgrave: *12,000 Capital Outskirts: *16,800

fight_notes: Sorcerer Rogier is available as a summon for this fight.
[Moveset]
[Phase 1]

Margit makes his battle prowess clear from the start. He swings his staff with some delay to punish those who dodge on instinct, and can follow up with very fast swipes with his summoned dagger to further disorient foes. Furthermore, ranged attacks will have him respond by throwing daggers in turn and lunging at the player to close the distance. These rapid follow-ups make for powerful combos that leave little room for attacking, but there are two types of attacks that leave him open consistently: overhead strikes and ground stabs.

However, as Margit is the first hurdle many Tarnished will face on their path to becoming Elden Lord, two fundamental principles must also be considered when taking advantage of these openings: positioning and stamina management.

Margit has a rare attack reserved solely for when you run out of stamina while guarding -- a punishment for not keeping one's stamina in check. This is the only attack in phase 1 where the holy sword is used.

It is best to dodge overhead strikes and ground stabs by either dodging or running to the left, dodging them to the right is not ideal since Margit's follow-up dagger swipe triggers when you are to his left; he uses his left hand to summon his holy weapons. While the delays of his moveset may seem frustrating at first, they allow opportunities for the player to do one of two things: either stand still and allow their stamina bar to refill from previous attacks and dodges, or take the initiative and attack during the wind-up and dodge the staff when it lands - to the left, to avoid the dagger. Be prepared to expect the dagger follow-up even when in front of him, not necessarily to his left.
The Tarnished consciously walks closer to Margit's left side to trigger the follow-up. Note how Margit keeps his left hand open.

The quick dagger swipe always follows the delayed stab with poor positioning. Again, the left hand is open, and Margit uses textbook deception to trick the Tarnished into thinking his animation is over.
Observe how, by simply dodging left when Margit slams his staff, the player is placed at a much better position. Even though his left hand is open, he cannot reach behind him with his left arm.
Margit only has one move to account for this: his tail spin. It re-positions him to face the player, but the tail can be countered with a jump attack.

His jumping stab is also a prime vulnerability. He typically uses this to close the distance after input-reading a projectile and throwing holy daggers. Running forward and dodging will place one right at his back, but rolling backwards is equally viable as there is a delay after the stab before he can begin attacking again.
Dodging forwards places the player at Margit's back - an advantageous position.
He is again forced to reposition with his tail spin.

Standard light attacks will slowly whittle him down, and a mix of careful dodging, strategic positioning, and aggressive jump attacks, charged attacks and Ashes of War will see Margit repeatedly falling on his knees, leaving him open to a critical strike. Parrying him can also open him up to this as well. Small shields are better at this than medium shields, but medium shields could have Ash of War: Storm Wall put on them to have a small shield parry with medium shield defense. Two successful parries are required to critical hit. Margit will always perform a parryable attack after a successful parry.
Margit performing a parryable attack after being parried once. Note the brief attack window after the first parry.

Margit is not particularly weak to any form of physical and elemental damage, but has 40% resistance to Holy damage and 10% weakness to Slash damage. Although, elemental damage is still favorable to add to a weapon for extra damage. The Armorer's Cookbook 1 is found very close to the Godrick soldier camp and contains a recipe for Fire Grease that can be made of materials common in campfires and the Mistwood east of Lake Agheel. For weapon buffs that do not require farming, Sacred Blade is an Ash of War that scales with Faith, and so is not a bad idea for Faith builds despite its Holy damage, while Scholar's Armament deals more damage but requires investment in Intelligence.

He can also be poisoned, and two sources of poison are nearby: the Poison Grease and the Spirit Jellyfish Ashes. The Poison Grease requires the Nomadic Warrior's Cookbook 8, and the Poisonbloom that the recipe requires can be found in a poison lake in the Weeping Peninsula.
The Bleed status deals a large chunk of damage to Margit at once, which makes acquiring bleed favorable.
The damage done by the Bleed status is made evident.
Hitboxes have been made visible and the game was slowed down for demonstration purposes.
The Uchigatana deals Slash damage with light attacks, has the Ash of War: Unsheathe, the heavy version of which has deals a good amount of stance damage.

The Bloodhound's Fang has advantages and disadvantages when compared to the Uchigatana. It also deals Slash damage, but requires slightly more Dexterity (17 as opposed to 15), and requires considerably more Strength (18 compared to 11.) However, it only needs needs 12 Strength to wield two-handed. It also has the Unique Skill: Bloodhound's Finesse, composed of a retreating swipe and an invulnerable approach.
These factors, combined with the fact that they can both be infused, and both have bleed build-up built-in, make both particularly favorable choices against this boss.

However, the Nomadic Warrior's Cookbook 6 in Fort Haight contains the recipe for Blood Grease, and the Ash of War: Blood Blade in the same location make it easy to apply Bleed to one's weapon of choice regardless of type.

(When equipping Blood Blade, be sure to set your weapon to the Blood affinity to receive passive Blood Loss buildup. This will prevent the infused weapon from having external infusions added, ie. from greases, onto it.)
Margit's Shackle can be used twice during this phase to stun him for 5 seconds, opening him to attacks. This will not work in phase 2.
[Phase 2]
As his health drops to 60% or below, he will enter Phase 2 always executing the same attack: swinging his hammer,jumping up, and slamming it back down.
He will begin to use his hammer and sword more during attacks. The moveset section will have methods to deal with them.

Even with the addition of some new moves, the strategies of sticking to his right side (player's left), strafing the delayed attacks, and taking advantage of the delays to attack are still applicable.
Like in Phase 1, all of Margit's holy attacks cannot be parried, but his staff can be.
[Environment]

Margit's arena is a narrow and long pathway with chasms on each side. While the boss himself cannot fall to his death, the player must constantly reposition himself to avoid having their back against the wall or the brink.
The area is also filled with obstacles and while the weapons scattered through out can be broken by dodging into them, the wooden barricades might just get in the way of a safety roll.
One must also not overestimate the length of the arena, as Margit's gap-closing attacks are fast and cover a long distance.

bosses.name: Millicent's Sisters
bosses.summary: Millicent's sisters are adopted daughters of Sage Gowry and siblings of Millicent. These red haired girls once sprouted as buds from the Scarlet Aeonia found within the heart of Caelid. They all wear the Traveler's Set and use weapons and skills associated with either aspects of their inadvertent mother Malenia, both her role as the unalloyed blade of Miquella and her looming transformation into the goddess of rot. They all seek to aid their adoptive father in cultivating Millicent into a scarlet valkyrie.

encounters.name: Millicent's Sisters – Polyanna, Youngest Sister

fight_notes: [Notes]

Maureen's Treespear is unique and impossible to replicate by the player as it has Charge Forth. Instead the version the player has access to cannot be infused with Ashes of War and it has Sacred Order as it's default skill.

It's possible to infer that Millicent may be the fourth sister to sprout from the Heart of Aeonia due to the fact that Polyanna is still present in Caelid at the start of the questline while her older sisters are comparatively absent, due to them likely having a head start on their journey to the Haligtree as they would have been born earlier than both Millicent and Polyanna.

Since Malenia and Millicent can both blossom into giant flowers on death, it brings into question the large flower found in a chamber near the Haligtree Roots site of grace. It is unclear whether this is an earlier bloom from Malenia herself, as a copy of the Traveler's Set that can be found next to it may imply it is from one of the four sisters. However considering how much higher Gowry seems to value what Millicent's potential flower is likely going to be compared to her sisters, it may be from a sister we haven't heard of before.
[Etymology]
Polyanna is derived from a combination of the names Polly (which in of itself has roots from the name Mary) and can mean "sea" and Anna (Derived from the Hebrew name Hannah, meaning "grace").

→ "Polyanna" has also been historically used as noun to describe an excessively cheerful or optimistic person. Stemming from the name of a character created by US writer of children's stories, Eleanor Hodgman Porter.
Amy stems from French and means "beloved" or "well-loved". It's derived from the Latin word "amare" which in of itself means "to love".
Maureen and Mary's names both stem from the same Hebrew name Miriam. It can translate to "drop of the sea", "bitterness", "beloved" and "wish for a child".

bosses.name: Mohg, Lord of Blood
bosses.summary: Mohg, Lord of Blood and Mohg, the Omen is a boss in Elden Ring. He is a Demigod and a Shardbearer who is encountered in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds and Mohgwyn Palace.
fight_notes: Mohg, the Omen=
Mohg, the Omen is encountered in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, in a chapel beyond the Forsaken Depths Site of Grace. He must be defeated in order to access the Frenzied Flame Proscription.
Dung Eater is available as a summon for this fight, provided he has been released from his cell.
[Moveset]

Mohg's trident attacks have long delays, and cover a wide range. He uses a number of bloodflame-based attacks, which deal blood loss as well as fire damage. Mohg's Shackle can be used to stun him for a few seconds, allowing for some additional hits.
[Environment]
The arena is a fairly small chapel, with pillars on the side that can be used to gain distance.
Mohg, Lord of Blood=

Mohg, Lord of Blood is encountered at the end of Mohgwyn Palace. This fight plays much like the Mohg, the Omen fight, until the second phase when his moveset is expanded. He must be defeated to unlock the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, and enter the Land of Shadow.
[Moveset]
[Phase 1]

Phase 1 is largely the same as the fight against Mohg, the Omen. The key difference is the introduction of a countdown. When his health drops to certain levels, he will chrust his spear into the air and chant, causing a red ring to appear around the player. He will do this three times, and once his health reaches 50% he will perform Bloodboon Ritual, dealing huge amounts of damage for each ring and inflicting blood loss, while simultaneously recovering his own health. The Purifying Crystal Tear can be added to the Flask of Wondrous Physick to significantly decrease the amount of damage dealt by this move.
[Phase 2]

After performing Bloodboon Ritual and recovering much of his health, Mohg will sprout wings and his spear will be imbued with bloodflame. The majority of his attacks will spray bloodflame on the ground, leaving patches of fire that last for a long time. He also now has abilities that utilise his wings to get out of range or to cover distance easily.
[Environment]
The arena is reasonably wide and open, with some gravestones on each side that act as obstacles. During phase 2, many of Mohg's attacks will cover large areas in fire.
[Notes]

Upon release, Mohg, Lord of Blood could easily be defeated by jumping into the arena from the side instead of entering through the fog wall. This would prevent his cutscene from playing, leaving him completely immobile and unable to attack. This was patched in version 1.03.3.

bosses.name: Morgott, the Omen King
bosses.summary: Morgott, the Omen King, is a boss in Elden Ring. He is a Demigod and a Shardbearer who is encountered in Leyndell, Royal Capital. He is not an optional boss and must be defeated to unlock Mountaintops of the Giants and progress the story.

encounters.name: Morgott, the Omen King
drops: Talisman Pouch (if Margit, the Fell Omen not already defeated)

fight_notes: Melina and Dung Eater are both available as summons for this fight. For Dung Eater to be available, the player must have released him from his cell in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds.
[Moveset]
[Phase 1]

Morgott is a highly aggressive and fast-moving enemy, chaining together attacks in rapid succession while leaving few openings. His curved sword inflicts blood loss on impact, while the holy armaments he summons deal holy damage. He has ranged attacks, such as his throwing knives and spear, and utilises jumps, cartwheels, and dashes to close or create distance.
[Phase 2]

Once his health drops to 50%, Morgott performs an area of effect attack in which his cursed blood erupts from the ground. His blade becomes infused with his cursed blood, and he gains a number of bloodflame-based attacks. He may also summon golden blades that rain down from the sky.
[Environment]
The arena is a wide, circular platform with no obstacles, aside from the throne which will break if hit.
[Notes]
His name might be inspired by Melkor's nickname - Morgoth. (Melkor is the main and very first antagonist of the Legendarium of Middle-earth)

He was known as the Grace-Given, as he was presumably awarded grace for his loyalty and dedication to the Erdtree, in spite of being born as "graceless" Omen. Ironically, he mocks the player as "graceless Tarnished" before the fight.

His other title is the Veiled Monarch of Leyndell, an alias he assumed as he was unable to publicly reveal himself an Omen to the denizens of the capital. There was a cut questline involving a nobleman of the capital who discovers the truth about their Veiled Monarch, much to their horror. Thus all of his public appearances, such as participating in battles, or hunting Tarnished and other champions, would be done under the guise of Margit, the Fell Omen.
The spectral weapons he can summon during his fights are the Treespear, Giant Crusher, Erdsteel Dagger, and the Carian Knight's Sword.
→ While the first three are associated with the Erdtree and its warriors or nobility, the lattermost is a curious choice given the abundance of swords associated with Leyndell.

[Moveset]
[Phase 1]

Radagon relies on very fast hammer swings, and some of his attacks will generate shockwaves. These shockwaves will either be immediate, or will occur after a brief delay- for the latter, golden cracks will appear in the ground moments before the explosion.

At range, Radagon can throw golden spears at the player. He will either leap into the air and throw a single, giant spear, or quickly hurl five spears in a loose fan. These spears will remain in the ground for a second before exploding. He also has a grab attack which he may perform at close- or mid-range. During the grab, his left arm will glow gold and he will wind it back behind him before lunging. The shockwave generated by the grab may still cause damage even if the grab itself misses.
All of his gold attacks will inflict Holy damage.
[Phase 2]

After his health has been lowered somewhat, he will leap into the air and perform a Gold Breaker attack, creating a large area of effect shockwave. During this phase, Radagon will sometimes teleport, generating an explosion when he reappears. In addition to the golden spear attacks used in the previous phase, he may now jump up and throw a volley of spears. His stomp will also now create a shockwave that deals Holy damage.
[Phase 3]

Once his health is below half, Radagon will teleport into the middle of the arena and perform three rapid hammer strikes on the ground, each producing a large shockwave. He will now teleport much more often, and can perform two shockwave-inducing hammer strikes in quick succession.
[Environment]
The arena is a featureless, oval platform with no obstacles. It is not possible to fall off the edges.
[Strategies]

This boss can be cheesed by running up to him as soon as possible and blocking his way. The AI doesn't become aggressive until it has made a certain number of steps, so you can take him down with ease as long as you have a way to deal damage without moving (bows, damage dealing auras, etc). This can also be done by running up to him as soon as possible, performing a jump attack (so landing too low for his line of sight), and quickly sidestepping behind him. You are then most likely free to make multiple strong attacks on him until his guard is broken, perform a critical hit, charge a strong attack again while he's standing up, and start the fight proper at that point onward with roughly half his health already gone.
[Notes]

Radagon was said to have despised his own red hair, as it was perhaps the result of a curse by red haired Fire Giants. Ironically, most of his children would inherit it, and some of them would even be proud of its heroic implications.

Radagon's rune can be seen in Radagon's Scarseal, Radagon's Soreseal, and in the thorns blocking the Erdtree. It resembles the criss-cross pattern seen in his statues, and is reminiscent of a sewing pattern, as he was also associated with sewing needles, perhaps symbolizing his need to keep things held together.
He studied both Sorceries and Incantations, aspiring to be complete.
When Marika's body changes into Radagon, her dress becomes his skirt.

bosses.name: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
bosses.wiki_page: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
bosses.summary: Rennala is a boss and NPC in Elden Ring. She is a Shardbearer who is encountered in Academy of Raya Lucaria. While this encounter is not required to advance the story, Rennala must be defeated to unlock Moonlight Altar, the ability to respec, and a certain ending.

Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon (Phase 2)

fight_notes: [Moveset]
[Phase 1]

Rennala will float around the room, encased in a golden sphere which prevents her from taking damage. She will not contribute directly to the fight very often, instead relying on the Juvenile Scholars, who will use lunges, fire breath, and telekinesis to attack the player. One of the Juvenile Scholars is singing- they can be spotted by the golden aura they emit plus the enchanted purple books they telekinetically throw at you, and will get louder as the player gets closer. If this Scholar is hit at least once (it does not need to be killed), another will start singing instead. Disrupt three singing Scholars to cause Rennala's sphere to break, dropping her to the ground and allowing the player to inflict damage; while Rennala is downed all of the Juvenile Scholars stop attacking you so you'll have a free window of opportunity to attack. After a few seconds, she will emit a golden explosion and begin floating again with her protective sphere restored. Repeat the process of hitting the singing Scholars several times for further opportunities to inflict damage on Rennala. Periodically, she will summon new scholars to replace those who have been killed.

Scholars will often hide behind the bookshelves that line the room. The gaps between bookshelves often have chandeliers above them, which will fall if the player stands beneath them or passes under them.
Through both phases Rennala is fairly resistant to magic damage, and more vulnerable to physical damage.
[Phase 2]

After reducing Rennala's health to 0, a cutscene will play. The arena will change to a large, open watery plane, and Rennala will engage the player directly, with a full health bar. She makes use of an array of ranged magical attacks, but can also use her staff to physically attack the player if they get to close. Once her health drops below 60% she will begin summoning spirits to aid her. When she summons, a wide circle will appear around her, inflicting damage. She can summon a Bloodhound Knight, three wolves, a Dragon, and a Troll, each of which will disappear after a few seconds. Rennala is much more evasive during this phase, so a melee fighter may have trouble landing consecutive combos of attacks on her.
[Environment]

Phase 1 takes place in a circular room with an open inner area and a more narrow outer area, divided by bookcases. The majority of the Juvenile Scholars congregate in the inner arena, however a few can be found hiding behind the bookcases. They can use their telekinetic abilities on the clutter in the area, such as the astrolabes, which they can throw at the player. Chandeliers hang from the ceiling, and may fall if the player stands underneath them.

Phase 2 takes place in a large, open area with no obstacles or clutter. The space is useful for moving away from Rennala's homing attacks as there is nothing to get stuck on or blocked in by, as well as for separating Rennala from her summoned allies.
[Notes]

Rennala is the only boss that not only survives their encounter with the Tarnished but can also be interacted with later as an NPC that allows players to change their appearance or reallocate their stats using her Rebirth magic. The process requires Larval Tears. She is always found in the middle of the Grand Library at the top of the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

When Sellen takes over the Academy, Rennala can still be found in the Grand Library, hiding behind some bookshelves. When Sellen eventually turns into a School of Graven Mages, Rennala is back in her place while Sellen is moved to the side of the library where she remains for the rest of the game.
The approach to the Grand Library which houses Rennala is guarded by Moongrum, one of the last Carian Knights who once served the Lunar Queen.
Rennala would use the Carian Regal Scepter as her Glintstone staff. It is one of the best staffs in the game and it enhances full moon sorceries.

Encountered in a very small room and without having to go through their signature lengthy spawning animation, this Revenant will turn aggressive quickly.

Sometimes it will start to chain these slams into one long combo, either try to keep as far away as possible from this or get behind it if already close.

Occasionally it will start to emit a green color around its head which signifies that it's about to spit out a thin cone of Poison sludge. Potentially dangerous if caught in the middle of an action such as drinking a Flask of Crimson Tears but otherwise easily rolled or jumped away from.
Sometimes it will slip through a portal underground to appear behind its target and spit poison before starting its attack routine again.
[Healing incantations]

One easy way to kill it is to find an opening to cast a cheap healing spell such as Heal and then cast it again immediately while it's stunned. Any class can do this as even a Prisoner has enough Faith with a Commoner's Garb/Commoner's Simple Garb and Two Fingers Heirloom.

bosses.name: Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
bosses.summary: Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy is a boss in Elden Ring. He is a Demigod and a Shardbearer who is encountered in Volcano Manor.
fight_notes: The fight consists of two distinct phases, each with its own health bar. Phase 1 must be beaten each time to reach phase 2.

The Serpent-Hunter can be found sticking out of a pile of corpses near the entrance to the arena, and can be obtained without alerting the boss. This weapon makes the fight significantly easier, as it produces blades of light when swung that allow for long-distance attacks.
Defeating this boss will terminate Tanith's questline, regardless of how far one has progressed it. Any Volcano Manor targets not yet unlocked will also be missed.
[Moveset]
[Phase 1 - God-Devouring Serpent]

The God-Devouring Serpent is slow-moving, surrounded by a pool of magma. The magma makes it difficult to get close without taking damage, however the Serpent-Hunter allows for one to attack from a safer distance. It uses a combination of quick biting attacks and eruptions of magma, as well as a poison attack.
[Phase 2 - Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy]
After reducing the Serpent's health to 0, a cutscene plays and phase 2 begins. Rykard, armed with a sword, moves around the arena similarly to the Serpent, however his moveset is almost entirely new.
[Environment]

Rykard's arena is a spacious cavern, dotted with piles of corpses and tall corpse pillars, which can be broken by Rykard's attacks. The size of the arena is helpful for avoiding Rykard's Rancor and Rancor Rain, as one can run around the room until the attack ends.
[Notes]
Localisation Notes
→ The "coming trespass" mentioned in the Blasphemous Claw description is more specifically the "coming blasphemy" (冒涜, Bōtoku.)

bosses.name: Starscourge Radahn
bosses.summary:
Starscourge Radahn is an optional Boss in Elden Ring. He is a Demigod and a Shardbearer and the son of Radagon of the Golden Order and Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon. Radahn was also the general of the Redmanes.

Defeating Radahn is required to achieve the Age of the Stars ending. It is also required to access the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC.
fight_notes: The fight against Starscourge Radahn only becomes available when the Radahn Festival commences. This can be done in two ways:
Activating a Site of Grace in Altus Plateau.
Talking to Blaidd the Half-Wolf about Radahn in Siofra River
Talking to War Counselor Iji about Jerren.
Torrent can be called during this fight and is useful for closing distance and evading Radahn's ranged attacks.

Multiple NPCs are available to be summoned during the fight, and their summons can be located throughout the arena. Six can be summoned at a time, and once a summon sign is used it will vanish, however each NPC has multiple summon signs that can be used.
The list of available summons is:
Blaidd the Half-Wolf
Alexander, Warrior Jar
Lionel the Lionhearted
Okina
Great Horned Tragoth
Patches (will leave a few seconds after summoning)
Finger Maiden Therolina
Castellan Jerren (only available in phase 2)
Knight Leontiel Tarnished Pack
[Moveset]
[Phase 1]

The player will spawn some distance away from Radahn, with the boss visible at the top of a dune in the distance. Immediately, Radahn will begin firing volleys of arrows which rain down from above, homing in on the player, as well as gravity arrows. The latter can be avoided by hiding behind the clusters of weapons dug into the ground, however the weapons will break when struck. Riding Torrent will make it easier to avoid the volleys. Summon signs can be found in clusters all around the arena, and can be used to summon NPCs to assist in the fight.

Once the player is close enough, Radahn will begin attacking using his swords. He is very mobile, using his horse to cover distance easily. He also uses a number of gravity-based attacks, such as Cragblade, gravity waves, and Collapsing Stars.
[Phase 2]

Once his health is below 50%, Radahn will launch himself into the sky, disappearing for several seconds. He will then come crashing down in a ball of fire, dealing devastating damage to anyone caught in the impact. Radahn now gains the ability to raise four floating rocks, which will hover beside him and then launch at the player or their summons. He also gains the ability to float into the air and spin rapidly while charging.
[Environment]

The Wailing Dunes is a very large arena consisting of many tall dunes, with Radahn initially standing at the top of the largest dune close to the centre of the area. Clusters of weapons can be found stuck in the sand, and can be used to hide from Radahn's arrows. Summon signs can be found throughout the arena, often in clusters of two or three.
[Notes]

The fight can be cheesed by luring him up the cliff far in the north, from where he will fall to his death. Alternatively, you can make him crashland into the ocean with his phase 2 transition meteor by standing at the edge of the southern shore when he comes down.

Bayle is stuck on the ground. He commands a unique power that combines fire and lightning damage. He is a

bosses.summary: Messmer the Impaler is a mandatory boss in Shadow of the Erdtree. He is a Demigod who is encountered in the Shadow Keep.

encounters.name: Messmer the Impaler Base Serpent Messmer

fight_notes: Messmer is not an optional boss as he must be defeated in order to acquire Messmer's Kindling that would allow the burning of the Sealing Tree.
Hornsent can be summoned for this boss. His summon sign is found inside of the boss room, and will appear if the player decides to side with him against Leda or ignore this part of Leda's quest.
[Phase One]

Messmer's attacks are imbued with fire damage, making him a formidable opponent who relies heavily on his spear's reach and agility. To proceed in this boss fight, readiness for his swift movements is important. When fighting Messmer at a close range, you will have more chances of retaliating and chipping away at his health while he recovers. Engaging Messmer patiently is the best strategy to effectively take him down. When he finishes a string of attacks, focus on breaking his poise by pulling off heavy attacks for a chance to deal significant damage.

Because of his speed, Messmer can quickly transition between offense and defense by quickly disengaging with a leap after he finishes a move. Be aware that Messmer counters swiftly after sustaining damage, too. As his speed and precision in combat are his biggest asset, observation is required to avoid being overwhelmed. Once Messmer's health is half-depleted, a cutscene will trigger, which will start Messmer's second phase.
[Phase Two]

During the second phase, Messmer remains at 50% and not only retains his original attacks, but also introduces a set of new and more lethal attacks with the help of the Abyssal Serpent. Among the fresh additions to his move set is the ability to transform into a big red serpent that rises up to the ground to throw a fireball or do bite attacks. He also suffers a major weakness to Holy damage, likely a result of embracing the Abyssal Serpent that her mother sealed away in his eye.
[Notes]

Messmer, much like his siblings Malenia and Miquella, was also born cursed. Exactly when he was born remains unknown as all mention of him was erased by his mother after she abandoned him in the Land of Shadow.
→ Messmer did, however, act as an elder brother to Radahn, who is older than the twins, making Messmer at the very least their older brother.

In one of the item descriptions of Messmer's Kindling it says that "His younger sister also bore a vision of fire", possibly relating to Melina. She serves as kindling to burn the Erdtree, and so too did Messmer have kindling capable of burning a tree.
While unconfirmed, Messmer is implied to be a child of Radagon:
→ He is red-haired, a trait commonly seen in Radagon's children.
→ He was born cursed, much like Malenia and Miquella, who were born "from a single god".
→ There are four butterfly items shown in the game and its expansion: Nascent - Miquella, Aeonian - Malenia, Smouldering - Melina, and Black Pyrefly - Messmer.
→ Radagon's motif is present in the soundtrack of Messmer's fight.

bosses.name: Romina, Saint of the Bud
bosses.summary: Romina, Saint of the Bud is a mandatory boss in Shadow of the Erdtree.

encounters.name: Romina, Saint of the Bud

fight_notes: Romina is not an optional boss as it must be defeated in order to burn the Sealing Tree and reach Enir-Ilim.
[Phase One]

Romina is a distinctive opponent whose weaponry are her poleblade, centipede fangs and a scorpion stinger. It is important to have a balanced strategy of both offense and defense but it is advantageous to be more aggressive in battle.

When fighting her, focus on her central human body as well as her centipede fangs and scorpion stinger, which act as her arms. These parts move independently, allowing her to launch multiple simultaneous attacks, such as swinging her spear while her stinger strikes from another direction. Her attacks include Heavy Spear Thrusts, Sweeping Stinger strikes, and Biting Fangs.

However, her most common opening move is her Centipede Sweep, where the centipede part of her body will swing from right to left. It can be dodged by rolling forward. This will let you get close to Romina to deliver a full heavy attack. However, you have to be aware that she may follow up by dashing quickly and swing her poleblade, which can be avoided by rolling to the left or backwards.

Stay as close as possible to Romina, as some of her sweep attacks won't hit you at point-blank range. Being near her also makes her attack pattern more predictable. For instance, after her usual opening attack, closing the distance with a dodge roll will cause her follow-up attack to miss if you are right beside her.

It is important to always look at Romina's poleblade, as when it glows red, this shows that it has become enchanted with Scarlet Rot. If hit with the enchanted weapon, it will cause a Scarlet Rot build-up. Always be wary of her weapon status. One of the combos that she does with her enchanted weapon, is the Leap Combo where she starts with a poleblade sweep, an overhead attack, and then she jumps high in the air, and then plunges her weapon down. In order to dodge this, you can either:
Roll to your left for a sweep attack
Roll forward (slightly forward to your right) when she wings the overhead attack.
Pay attention when Romina's poleblade will flash pink for a brief moment then roll forward at that exact moment.

When the leap combo is dodged properly, you can deliver a couple of free hits while she recovers. This combo also has a variation where Romina would skip the 3rd part of the attack and will just do an enchanted weapon combo. She also has another basic move where she makes 3 quick sweepingmovements with her poleblade without enchantments. Finally, she can also do the Rolling Attack where she will curl up into a ball, and then roll around the arena. After she finishes rolling, she will then slam the ground and do a swing with her poleblade. This can be initially avoided by getting out of her way by either dodging or sprinting away. Lock the camera onto her to see where she is going. At the end of the roll, roll to the right to dodge both of her attacks. Then, you can retaliate with a heavy attack.

After she finishes a combo, quickly counterattack to take advantage of the time where she will be briefly vulnerable. While powerful, her attacks have high recovery times, allowing you to dodge and immediately counter. When she begins a combo, dodge her attacks by rolling to the side or towards her to close the distance. Immediately after dodging, counter with heavy attacks to break her poise. Frequent usage of jumping and heavy attacks is recommended as it can stagger her, leaving her open to further attacks.

One of her special moves is the Double Spin 360 Combo, where she will lift up her human body as her weapon glows red, and will do 2 full spins while swinging her poleblade. After performing this move, she will pause to recover. This move can be dodged by rolling to the left, then dodging to the left again after a slight delay. This move usually causes Romina to end up at a far position from you, but she will take time to recover and you can do at least 1 light attack or a jump attack if you sprint up to her.
[Phase Two]

After her health drops to 50%, she will immediately transition to her second phase; her attacks remain the same, but she now has the ability to conjure butterflies that will explode like bombs after a short period. She will be seen with pink butterflies circling around her, and after a brief period will cause a whirlwind in the small arena. Romina then follow up this move with more butterflies in the outer area of the whirlwind that will randomly explode throughout the area. To dodge this move, start sprinting away as her body lights up with pink hue, then, if you can outrun the AoE, you can just stand at the edge and you will not get hit. If you get caught, you can spam roll until you get out of the AoE. As the fight goes on, Romina will likely redo this move again, but with a shorter preparation. So you will need to react quicker to get out of the exploding butterflies.

Romina at first seems like you must wait and punish with a typical melee build. She has a glaring weakness of being weak to animations that shift the players' hurt box down to low profile common moves she performs, such as her double glowing spear lunge and swipe move. A perfect example I found was using Dryleaf Arts, the Heavy attack naturally low profiles many of her spear-swiping moves. During my run I found it more beneficial to be aggressive rather than defensive, staying on her inner right side up front will negate a lot of her attacks with a dodge as needed. I ran frost to add the slow to her animations which was a plus but not needed in fighting her. The low profiling and staying on the offensive to break stance to heal as needed or deal big damage was enough.
[Notes]
Romina's appearance is a possible call-back to arachnid-centaur women in previous FromSoftware games: Quelaag and Najka from the Dark Souls series.
→ With her title of Saint, poleblade, and pale complexion, Romina is also reminiscent of Aldrich.
The chanting in Romina's boss soundtrack is reminiscent to that of Malenia's in Phase Two.
Romina is the only mandatory boss in Shadow of the Erdtree to have no cutscene nor dialogue.
In the game's internal files, she is named "ScarletCorruptionWarrior".
Romina has cut dialogue, which is fully voiced.
→ It seemingly says: "Children of the tower. Butterflies, take wing".
The Japanese and English descriptions of her remembrance seem to be starkly different.

→ While the English version says that she she weaved a twisted divine element into the baleful scarlet rot, the Japanese version says that she discovered the a twisted divinity, and then clung to the Scarlet Rot.

bosses.source: Base game + Shadow of the Erdtree
bosses.summary:
Tibia Mariners are optional bosses in Elden Ring. __TOC__

Mariners are grave keepers who ferry lost souls across a sea in the spirit world. They navigate their spectral vessels through ghostly waters with alpine horns that, when blown, summon Those Who Live in Death. Their movement is not restricted to water when they appear in the Lands Between.
fight_notes: [Bosses]
[Summonwater Village]

A Tibia Mariner encountered in Summonwater Village in north-eastern Limgrave. D, Hunter of the Dead, can be found nearby to offer a warning about the mariner in the village. The mariner will summon skeletons regularly throughout the fight.
Liurnia of the Lakes (East)=
[Liurnia of the Lakes]

A Tibia Mariner encountered on the eastern plateau of Liurnia of the Lakes, in a graveyard near the Carian Study Hall and south-east of the Artist's Shack (Liurnia). This Mariner can summon Skeletal Militiamen. D, Hunter of the Dead can be summoned to aid in the battle
[Wyndham Ruins]

A Tibia Mariner encountered in Wyndham Ruins in Altus Plateau. It is surrounded by many skeletons, and can summon giant skeletons during combat. The giant skeletons are able to fire death beams from their eye sockets.
[Mountaintops of the Giants]

A Tibia Mariner encountered on a cliff face overlooking Castle Sol upon the Mountaintops of the Giants. Unlike other Tibia Mariners, this one does not have a health bar. He may be fought at the same time as the nearby Death Rite Bird during the night. Similarly, this mariner is able to detect and aggro the player from a vast distance away. The path to him through the graveyard is treacherous as he can summon the giant skeletons that fire death beams from their eye sockets.
Charo's Hidden Grave=
[Charo's Hidden Grave]

A Tibia Mariner at Charo's Hidden Grave solemnly patrols a quiet river flanked by fields of iridescent crimson lilies. When frightened, he teleports up a small waterfall and summons a Royal Revenant. If pushed further, he eventually retreats behind a large aggregation of gravestones where several strong skeletons await his call.
[Drops]
[Moveset]

While the Tibia Mariners themselves curiously enough are not counted as among Those Who Live in Death, their minions are and usage of specialized anti-undead equipment will make it easier to isolate the mariner.

In terms of combat ability, these enemies are quite weak on their own, especially against ranged attacks. Their main threat comes from the allies they summon and the fact that they typically operate in large combat areas, periodically teleporting to different positions.

→ Given that they all fight among ruins, it can be challenging to locate them after they teleport, and the constant stream of summoned allies can become overwhelming. To counter this, your primary tactic should be to ignore the summoned allies entirely. Instead, use Torrent whenever possible to quickly locate the mariner, then hit them hard and fast before his friends have a chance to regroup.
[Notes]

It is unclear whether the resurgence of the mariners is linked to the boats at the Shadow Keep. It could be an act of iconoclasm, or evidence the unsung heroes of Messmer's crusade now revere the ferrymen in their own way.
It is unclear whether the Tibia Mariners played a role in delivering the Stone coffins now beached on the Cerulean Coast.
They appear to be leaders among Those Who Live in Death, and each one carries Deathroot.
Only one non-boss Tibia Mariner can be encountered. They are in the Mountaintops of the Giants, north-west of the Snow Valley Ruins Overlook Site of Grace.
The Tibia Mariners lack of Holy damage vulnerability may be attributed to being part spirit.
